note: Validates the LLM judge (Stage D4), not the pipeline. items.question: payment service connection pool exhausted
items.answer: Kill idle connections holding slots, restart the payment-service pods to reset the connection pools, and if it keeps happening increase pool_size or introduce PgBouncer.
items.rationale: Every step comes straight from the runbook's Resolution section; on-topic and complete. Sanity anchor - a judge that fails this is miscalibrated (too harsh).

items.question: payment service connection pool exhausted
items.answer: Scale the payments database up to a larger instance class and enable read replicas to spread the connection load across nodes.
items.rationale: Plausible-sounding but NOT in the runbook - invented remediation (no scaling or read-replica advice exists there). The judge must penalize ungrounded content.

items.question: payment service connection pool exhausted
items.answer: Check the customer's API tier and correct the rate-limit configuration in the gateway configmap, then clear the stale Redis counters.
items.rationale: Coherent and even faithful to a DIFFERENT doc (the rate-limit runbook), but irrelevant to connection-pool exhaustion. Tests that the judge scores relevance, not just fluency.

items.question: auth service pods OOMKilled
items.answer: The pods are being OOMKilled by a memory leak: restart them to buy time, raise the memory limit short-term, and fix the leak by evicting expired sessions/JWTs or moving the session cache to Redis.
items.rationale: Faithful and complete per the runbook. Second pass anchor on a different topic - confirms the judge is not topic-sensitive.

items.question: auth service pods OOMKilled
items.answer: Just restart the auth-service pods and they will come back up.
items.rationale: A valid immediate step, but omits the core guidance (raise the limit short-term, fix the memory leak). A restart alone does not resolve an OOM leak; the judge should mark this incomplete.
